newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Strong crown hits Esselte '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Strong crown hits Esselte '96 profit.

text.p: Swedish office supplier Esselte AB on Friday reported a 12 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profit, despite a stronger crown eating into sales revenue.

Pre-tax profit rose to 667 million crowns ($95.6 million) from 594 million a year earlier, which was in line with market expectations. Sales revenue for the year slipped to 11.63 billion crowns from 12.15 billion.

But Esselte said based on comparable exchange rates, sales rose two percent in the first three quarters of the year and climbed six percent in the final three months with newly acquired units accounting for more than half of the late growth.
"For the fifth year in a row we increased our earnings and reached our goals," said Esselte chief executive Bo Lundquist in a statement.
"Since we are working on strengthening our balance sheet and have good control over costs, we see no barriers to increasing our earnings further in line with our goals," he said.
Lundquist said the results were good despite the stronger Swedish currency and weaker key European markets.
"After foreign currency translations, the higher value of the Swedish crown reduced income before tax by 46 million crowns...compared with last year," Lundquist said.
Markets in central and western Europe had not been favourable. "Particularly in France and Germany, which together account for 23 percent of group sales," he said.
The group's office products division posted an operating income of 461 million crowns compared to 465 million in 1995.
However, sales in the division -- the group's largest -- increased with the stronger crown taken into account.
"Sales of the office products business area increased slightly more than five percent in 1996, based on comparable exchange rates," the company said.
Lundquist said the company looked to 1997 with confidence.
"We will continue to expand within office products and our other business areas are also ready to start their growth processes," he said.
Sales in North America, Britain, southern Europe and the Nordic region -- with the exception of Sweden -- were strong.
The company's dividend will be announced on February 20.
-- Abigail Schmelz, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1003 ($1=6.977 Swedish Crown)
